Committee: Judiciary
Sponsor: Gudger
Analyst: Pete Grogan
Date: 03/08/2022
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 282 as introduced could decrease receipts to municipalities by an undetermined amount dependent upon the amount of municipal traffic fines and penalties collected in excess of 10% of the municipality's general operating budget. This bill could correspondingly increase receipts to the Crime Victim's Compensation Fund and the Fair Trail Tax Fund, equally, by an undetermined amount dependent on the amount of municipal traffic fines and penalties collected in excess of 10% of the municipalities most recently completed year's budget and subsequently transferred to these funds, as provided by this bill.
Tom Whatley, Chairperson
Judiciary

Senate Bill 282 as introduced could decrease receipts to municipalities by an undetermined amount dependent upon the amount of municipal traffic fines and penalties collected in excess of 10% of the municipality's general operating budget. This bill could correspondingly increase receipts to the Crime Victim's Compensation Fund and the Fair Trail Tax Fund, equally, by an undetermined amount dependent on the amount of municipal traffic fines and penalties collected in excess of 10% of the municipalities most recently completed year's budget and subsequently transferred to these funds, as provided by this bill.

FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 282 as passed the Senate could decrease receipts to municipalities by an undetermined amount dependent upon the amount of municipal traffic fines and penalties collected in excess of 10% of the municipality's general operating budget. This bill could correspondingly increase receipts to the Crime Victim's Compensation Fund and the Fair Trail Tax Fund, equally, by an undetermined amount dependent on the amount of municipal traffic fines and penalties collected in excess of 10% of the municipalities most recently completed year's budget and subsequently transferred to these funds, as provided by this bill.
In addition, this bill exempts Class 1 municipalities from the provisions of this bill.
Chris Pringle, Chair
